preconditions.description: The galaxy has between 1 and 100 planets, and between 0 and 10000 wormholes.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each wormhole connects two planets within the valid range.
The number of spaceships and bases are between 1 and 1000, and k and h are non-negative integers up to 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 0 <= a <= 10**9 and 0 <= f <= 10**9 for x, a, f in spaceships)
preconditions.description: Each spaceship has a valid planet location, attack strength, and fuel.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 0 <= d <= 10**9 for x, d in bases)
preconditions.description: Each base has a valid planet location and defense strength.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the minimum gold lost.

postconditions.expression: cost == min((b_attacked * k) + (dummy_bases * h) for b_attacked in range(0, min(s, b) + 1) for dummy_bases in range(0, s + 1) if (b_attacked + dummy_bases) <= s and (b - b_attacked) <= b_attacked + dummy_bases)
postconditions.description: The cost is the minimum gold lost, considering all possible ways to assign spaceships to real and dummy bases, where dummy bases are always attacked and real bases are attacked only if feasible.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= b_attacked <= min(s, b) and 0 <= dummy_bases <= s for b_attacked, dummy_bases in feasible_assignments)
postconditions.description: The feasible assignments of spaceships to real and dummy bases respect the constraints that no spaceship attacks more than one base and no base is attacked by more than one spaceship.
